chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) did not fast the Day of Arafah since the fasting of the month of Ramadan was revealed. So this does not contradict the first two narrations, because the narration only implies that the Prophet (peace be upon him) did not fast it, and it is permissible that the Prophet (peace be upon him) did so due to an excuse, even though it has merit, because the merit of fasting this day is specific to one who is strong upon it and it does not weaken him from supplication and asking [of God]. For it is a day of supplication and asking. As for one who is not strong upon it, it is better for him to break the fast. This indicates that.

key_terms.صِيَامُ شَهرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad not fast the Day of Arafah and is it better to fast or break the fast on this day?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Ishtibār highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) consistent non-fasting of Arafah post-Ramadan was likely due to a specific excuse rather than abrogation of its merit. It emphasizes that the day’s primary purpose is supplication, so fasting is recommended only if it does not impair one’s ability to engage in du'a, making breaking the fast preferable for those weakened by it. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on balancing physical worship with spiritual presence.
